extraction.name: MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI
extraction.description: MMMU is a benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering. These questions span 30 subjects and 183 subfields, comprising 30 highly heterogeneous image types.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.citeAs: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen. MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI. arXiv preprint arXiv:2311.16502v4, 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data is primarily collected from free online resources, quizzes, textbooks, and other study materials. Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the 30 subjects assisted in question collection. They collected multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary. The annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations, avoiding data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution. Given data contamination concerns, annotators were advised to select questions without immediately available answers, such as those with answers in separate documents or at the end of textbooks.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Document analysis, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions sourced from college exams, quizzes, textbooks, and online resources across 30 subjects spanning six disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data quality control was performed in multiple stages. In the first stage, lexical overlap and source URL similarity were employed to identify potential duplicate problems. Suspected duplicates were reviewed by authors to identify and eliminate duplications. The second stage involved distributing problems among co-authors for format and typo checking, ensuring adherence to a standardized format and undertaking necessary corrections. In the third stage, authors categorized problems into four difficulty levels: very easy, easy, medium, and hard. Approximately 10% of problems classified as very easy were excluded from the benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions were manually collected and annotated by over 50 university students specializing in the relevant subjects. Annotators categorized each question as either multiple-choice or open-ended, annotated all fields including question text, answer options, correct answer, image types, question difficulty, and explanation (if available). All questions were required to contain one or more images, be written in English, meet college-level difficulty, and be unambiguous. The annotation protocol included specific instructions for handling multiple-choice questions, open-ended questions, and questions with multiple images.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A user-friendly web interface was developed for data annotation and verification.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The paper includes a version change log documenting updates from v1 (Nov.27, 2023) through v4 (June 13, 2024), indicating ongoing maintenance and updates to model results and corrections.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark aims to push the boundaries of what large multimodal models can achieve and is intended to be instrumental in developing next-generation multimodal foundation models and monitoring progress towards Expert AGI. The authors caution that MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI but believe strong performance on it should be a necessary criterion for an Expert AGI system.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI. The benchmark combines multiple-choice questions with concise open-ended questions to balance complexity and practicality, but this may not capture all aspects of expert-level reasoning. Error analysis on GPT-4V revealed that 35% of errors are perceptual, 29% stem from lack of knowledge, and 26% are due to flaws in reasoning, highlighting challenges in visual perception, knowledge representation, and complex reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for evaluating multimodal models on college-level multi-discipline understanding and reasoning tasks. Use cases include testing models' capabilities in expert-level perception, knowledge recall, and reasoning across diverse domains. The benchmark is intended for zero-shot and few-shot evaluation of large multimodal models.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: For multiple-choice questions, one correct answer is annotated. For open-ended questions, one correct answer is provided. Explanations are included for 17.62% of questions (2,035 out of 11,550).
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 college students (including coauthors) from various disciplines and subjects served as annotators. Three student experts per subject (90 total) were involved in human expert evaluation.
